title: test: add CoreText bitmap font test
body:
Adds test coverage for bitmap font rendering in the CoreText backend, completing the CoreText side of #8524 (the FreeType side already landed in #10193).

The test uses an Apple bitmap-only SFNT (the `bhed` header table with `bdat`/`bloc` bitmap strikes) so it exercises the existing `bhed` fallback path in `getMetrics()`.

The test loads the font-face from memory, asserts the bhed-derived metrics, renders the 'A' glyph and checks it pixel by pixel againsts the expected bitmap, using the same approach used in the FreeType tests.

**Note on the font used:** `spleen-8x16-apple.ttf` it's the raw sfnt font data taken out of Spleen 2.1.0's `spleen-8x16.dfont` suitcase because CoreText can't load a dfont from memory but only a bare SFNT


**AI disclosure**: Senior Software Engineer here (7yoe), I'm working using AI with a spec driven approach, not vibe coding. Use it to derive the context, write the specs and implement what's needed being in the loop of every iteration checking manually every step and I'm happy to study what I don't know before doing any change. (as already stated in https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/13838)

Closes: https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/issues/8524

+## Notes
+
+`spleen-8x16-apple.ttf` is Spleen 8x16 as an Apple bitmap-only SFNT (it uses the `bhed` table rather than `head`), used only to test CoreText bitmap font support. CoreText can't load Spleen's `.dfont` from memory, so this file is the `sfnt` resource extracted from `spleen-8x16.dfont` in the Spleen 2.1.0 release — same font, version, and BSD 2-Clause license as the `spleen-8x16.{bdf,pcf,otb}` files.
